$$
(x + 1)=\sqrt{{t}^{2}-9},\,\,\,y=3{t}^{2},\,t\ge 3.
$$

The Cartesian equation of this curve is

$y=$
{{field-1}}$,\,(x + 1)\ge 0.$

To find the Cartesian equation, we eliminate $t.$ First, we use the $(x + 1)$ equation to solve for ${t}^{2}:$

$$

$$

Now, substituting ${t}^{2}={(x + 1)}^{2}+9$ into our expression for $y,$ we get

$$
y=3({(x + 1)}^{2}+9)=3{(x + 1)}^{2}+27.
$$

Finally, since $t\ge 3$ and $(x + 1)=\sqrt{{t}^{2}-9},$ we must have $(x + 1)\ge 0.$

Therefore, the complete Cartesian equation is $y=3{(x + 1)}^{2}+27,\,(x + 1)\ge 0.$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x - 2) & =\frac{1}{t-2} \\ (x - 2)(t-2) & =1 \\ t-2 & =\frac{1}{(x - 2)} \\ t & =\frac{1}{(x - 2)}+2 \\ t & =\frac{1+2(x - 2)}{(x - 2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now substituting $t=\frac{1+2(x - 2)}{(x - 2)}$ into our expression for $y={t}^{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={(\frac{1+2(x - 2)}{(x - 2)})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So the Cartesian equation of the given curve is $y={(\frac{1+2(x - 2)}{(x - 2)})}^{2}.$

Finally, since $t\ne 2$ and $(x - 2)=\frac{1}{t-2},$ we must have $(x - 2)\ne 0.$

So, the complete Cartesian equation is

$$
y={(\frac{1+2(x - 2)}{(x - 2)})}^{2},\,(x - 2)\ne 0.

y=\frac{(\frac{x - 9}{4})}{1-3(\frac{x - 9}{4})},\,(\frac{x - 9}{4})\ne 0,\,\frac{1}{3}.
$$
